findings: Gecko's actual text-control command callback performs controller lookup, availability checks and execution. Calling the editor directly would bypass the address field's custom copy/cut controller.

The packaged URL-bar controller formats complete URL copies, including protocol restoration and encoding, and owns its cut input-event behavior. Preserve it rather than implementing URL formatting or substituting generic EditorBase clipboard methods.

NativeUI's existing native menu/key interpreter supplies selectors through its text command capability and edit proposal. The adapter maps only semantic copy/cut/paste commands; no shortcut bindings, controls or clipboard content are copied.

Pure modifier presses were sent as empty keyDown text and deleted a selection. Use Gecko's own modifier classifier and the existing NXS_KEY_MODIFIERS event so actual AppKit receives flagsChanged. Keep the browser's modifier default action.
Physical compositor input is asynchronous. Test barriers observe the expected DOM keyup; acknowledge from the compositor alone does not prove browser processing.
A standalone Alt release activates Firefox's existing menu. Independent cases restore it with real Escape input and observe its inactive state, then focus the actual browser or address field.
Unfocused shared GPBS storage is not the current Wayland selection. A real focused native application imports the browser's formatted clipboard and provides the required cross-application evidence.
